summary: The root ذرأ primarily means to create, originate, or produce something from nothing, often referring to God's act of bringing forth creation.

provenance.lane: Edward William Lane, An Arabic-English Lexicon (1863-93), public domain. Digital text via Perseus, Tufts University, CC BY-SA 3.0 US.
provenance.summary: Editorial summary derived from the Lane entry. NOT Lane's own wording. Shown as a gloss only; the Lane text below is the source.

headwords.def: (T, S, M, &c.,) aor. َرَاَ, (S, M, Msb, K,) inf. n. َرْءٌ, (S, M, Msb,) He (God) created, syn. خَلَقَ, (T, S, M, Msb, K,) الخَلْقَ [ the creation; i. e. the things that are created ]. (T, S, M, Msb.) وَلَقَدْ َرَأْنَا لِجَهَنَّمَ كَثِيرًا مِنَ ٱلْجِنِّ وَ ٱلْإِنْسِ, in the Kur [vii. 178], means [ And verily ] we have created [ for Hell many of the jinn, or genii, and of mankind ]. (T.) He multiplied, or made numerous. (K.) يَ ْرَؤُكُمْ فِيهِ, in the Kur [xlii.

He angered him; provoked him to anger. (T, M, K.) ا رأهُ بِصَاحِبِهِ He incited him against his companion. (AZ, T.) And ا رأهُ بِالشَّىْءِ He incited him, or urged him, to do, or attempt, the thing. (M, K.) And ا رأهُ إِلَىكَ َا He constrained him, or compelled him, to have recourse to, or to do, such a thing. (K, * TA.) A 'Obeyd mentions أَ ْرَى, without ء; but 'Alee Ibn-Hamzeh asserts that this is incorrect. (M.) ا رأ الدَّمْعَ He, or it, made tears to flow.

The act of creating; inf. n. of َرَأَ. (S, M, Msb.) [And used in the sense of the pass. part. n. of that verb; and alike as sing. and pl. because originally an inf. n.] َرْءُ النَّارِ, (S, K, TA,) [for َرْءٌ لِلنَّارِ,] related as occurring in a trad. (S, TA) of 'Omar, (TA,) means Created [i. e.

(S, M, K) and, (S,) the latter an inf. n. (M, [see 1,]) the former a simple subst., (S,) Whiteness, or hoariness, in the fore part of the head: (S:) or whiteness intermixed with blackness in the hair of the head: (M:) or whiteness, or hoariness, of the hair: (K:) or the beginning of whiteness or hoariness (M, K) in the fore part of the head, (K,) or in the upper part of each side of the head. (A, TA.)
and َرَآنِىٌّ Intensely white salt: (S, M, K:) derived from ُرْأَةٌ: one should not say أَنْ َرَانِىٌّ; (S, K;) for this is a vulgarism: some pronounce it with the unpointed د. (TA.)

(T, S, M, Mgh, K) and ِرِّيَّةٌ (M, K) and َرِّيَّةٌ, (K,) [or َرِيَّةٌ, without a sheddeh to the ر, accord. to the Msb in art. ر,] always pronounced by the Arabs without ء: (S:) accord. to some, (TA,) from ال َّرْءُ; (M, TA;) so says Th; (M;) the measure of the first being فُعُّولَةٌ or فُعِّيلَةٌ; [so that it is originally ُرُّوءَةٌ or ُرِّيْئَةٌ;] (TA;) but the ء is suppressed because of frequency of usage: (M:) accord.
an epithet applied to God, The Creator. (T.)

; fem. َرْآءُ: see 1, last sentence. Applied to a ram, Having whiteness in the head; (M, K;) and so the fem. applied to a ewe: (M:) or having the ears variegated, or speckled, with black and white, and the rest black: (K:) or it has this latter meaning when applied to a horse, and to a kid; and so the fem. applied to a female kid, (S, O,) or to a she-goat: (M:) and is not applied to the sheep-kind. (S, O.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
mentions_note: Forms Lane discusses inside another entry rather than defining as a headword. Values index into headwords[].
